fixture.scope: fixed total series, per-slot shifts, last life may extend past nominal query end; not exact steady-state active-node simulation

method: Same stock O1 binary and same shifted fixture, two raw UUID TimeSeries SAMPLES bucket sizes3600/10800, 1 active part each after OPTIMIZE FINAL, merges stopped; four A/B/B/A phases per selector, 2 warmup+6 measured native PromQL queries each, strict full label/value/time parity and independent physical point/ID counts, source/manifest/binary SHA checked.
interpretation: Unaligned life shifts the number of samples bucket rows from aligned 86688/28896 to113760/57120 at3600/10800; the real ClickHouse physical counts match exact math.
Staggered namespace query at 10800s increases p50 15.8%, CPU 23.9%, vs A/A drift 1.68%, while physical read rows fall 30.1%. This strongly rejects a universal 10800s default.

Staggered namespace 10800s representative MergeTreeSelect work 89.2->122.4ms and read/decode CPU samples85->120; evidence is consistent with more expensive per-bucket decode or layout despite fewer read rows. Single-query profile samples are not a median or wall critical path proof.
Staggered broad pod p50 increases 5.2% with 2.5% drift; burst15 p50 increases13.8% with5.1% drift.
Staggered node_broad p50 improves3.9%, but its A/A drift is13.2%; inconclusive timing gain.
Compressed total storage still 6.6% smaller at10800, but compressed size alone does not determine CPU.
limits: Aligned baseline and staggered test ran on different GitHub runners: do not claim that the *difference* between their speedup ratios is causally caused by staggering until a 2x2 aligned/staggered same-runner factorial.
Queries read three-day daily grid and one-day avg_over_time lookback, not all PromQL matcher windows.
Single-client glibc O1 lab build, not production jemalloc, concurrency or 14d.
next_action: Same runner 2x2 factorial aligned/staggered x 3600/10800 bucket with full native parity and A/B/B/A to isolate interaction, then 4/8 clients or true steady-state HPA if promising.
